rapport_notes: Nicole is warm, professional, attentive to John's needs and preferences; paces well, confirms details clearly, and maintains friendly tone throughout.
process_discipline_notes: No repeats detected. Silence held after the agenda question. Clean handoff to walkthrough—no abandoned mid-stream pitch.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: I'll be asking some few questions and this call will just take around ten to fifteen minutes and I'll be able to build you an accurate code sounds good.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: What are your biggest concerns and what are the most important things you want answers to on this call today?
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised: timing/availability, services, pricing. Nicole followed with: 'do you already have a preferred move date?' (timing) → 'September 25th' → 'OK, 26 or 27 works' (layered); probed garage depth ('two car or three car... how many items... can you still park two cars or just one?'); confirmed move scope ('we're moving two blocks away... not moving a lot of furniture'). Each concern got real follow-up.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Usually, for the home of your size, we send out four movers and two truck and we usually do a virtual walkthrough... So we can figure out how many truck and how many movers you'll be needing for this move.

top_strength: Nicole nailed the agenda question early, before any logistics probing, and then drilled down with genuine follow-ups on the customer's stated concerns (timing, services, scope) rather than pivoting to a pitch.
coaching_note: This call correctly routed to a walkthrough; however, Stage 1 discovery missed both differentiators (damage/careful-with and Meet Your Mover)—neither came up organically and neither was layered in as a discovery hook, so no Stage 2 takeaway was built either; plan to seed one or both in the walkthrough-scheduler pre-call or during the virtual tour so the full value stack lands before estimate.
